p01.why: The outermost block of the body declares the initializer's a again.

p02.why: The jump to case 2 skips the initialization of x, which is in scope at the label.

p03.why: The condition declares x = 3, control goes to case 3, and x is visible there.

p04.why: One switch has a default and the other covers every enumerator and is followed by a return, so -Wall gives no warning, and 1 + 3 is 4.

p05.why: char, an unscoped and a scoped enumeration, bool, long long, and a class with one conversion to int are all valid condition types, and each case value fits its promoted type.

p06.why: 1 and '\x01' are equal after conversion, so the switch has two equal case values.

p07.why: The jump to case 1 skips d, whose destructor is not trivial; Clang and EDG reject the label and GCC accepts it (Q-0041).

p08.why: A double condition is not an integer, enumeration, or suitable class type.

p09.why: Each label belongs to the innermost switch, so pick gives 0, 12, and 10 for the three calls.

p10.why: A case label must be inside a switch.

p11.why: The condition is evaluated one time, so calls is 1.

p12.why: The member function of a local class is a separate function, so its case label belongs to no switch.

p13.why: P has trivial construction and destruction and p has no initializer, so case 1 may skip it, and f(1) returns 7.

p14.why: green has no case and there is no default, so Clang and GCC warn under -Wall and -Werror rejects the program, while EDG gives no warning and the program runs.

p15.why: break leaves only the switch, and default adds 1 for i = 0 and i = 2.

p16.why: 1 and 2 match their cases and 3 goes to default.

p17.why: A pointer condition is not an integer, enumeration, or suitable class type.

p18.why: case 2 skips int x, a scalar with no initializer, and x is assigned 7 before it is read.

p19.why: x lives in a block that ends before case 2, so the jump skips nothing in scope.

p20.why: Two case labels have the value 1.

p21.why: case 0 falls through to case 1, so the results are 11, 10, and 100.

p22.why: S converts to int only by an explicit conversion function, which the condition does not use.

p23.why: The outermost block of the body declares the condition variable c again.

p24.why: The initializer declares x = 2, the condition is 4, and case 4 sets r to x.

p25.why: Both conversion functions convert to int, which is one type, so the condition is valid.

p26.why: For a scoped enumeration condition each case value must have that enumeration type, and 0 is an int.

p27.why: busy gives 1, and the value 7 matches no case and there is no default, so control reaches return -1.

p28.why: k is a parameter, so case k is not a constant expression.

p30.why: 300 fits the promoted type int, so it is a valid case value that a char never matches, and pick(44) goes to default.

p31.why: The jump to case 2 skips a whole block, which is allowed.

p32.why: S converts to both int and long, two different integer types.

p33.why: case 1 inside the while loop is a valid target; run(1) gives 1 then 12 and run(0) gives 11.

p34.why: The lambda body is a separate function, so its case label belongs to no switch.

p35.why: A switch may have at most one default label.

p36.why: No case matches 3 and there is no default, so control goes past the switch and r stays 5.
